See also: Côté, Côte, Coté, Cote, cote, coté, côté, costé, coste, Costé, and Coste

French

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]
Etymology tree
Latin costabor.
Old French coste
Middle French coste
French côte

    Inherited from Middle French coste, from Old French coste, borrowed from Latin costa.

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
    • IPA(key): /kot/
    • Audio:(file)
    • Audio (France (Agen)):(file)
    • Audio (France (Paris)):(file)
    • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
    • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
    • Audio (France (Lyon)):(file)
    • Audio (France (Somain)):(file)

    Noun

    [edit]

    côte f (plural côtes)

    1. rib (bone)
    2. hill, slope
    3. coast

    Derived terms

    [edit]
    • côte à côte
    • Côte d'Azur
    • Côte d'Ivoire
    • Côte d'Or
    • côtier
    • démarrage en côte
    • entrecôte

    Related terms

    [edit]
    • accoster
    • côté
    • intercostal

    Further reading

    [edit]
    • “côte”, in Trésor de la langue française informatisé [Digitized Treasury of the French Language], 2012

    Norman

    [edit]

    Etymology

    [edit]
    Etymology tree
    Latin costabor.
    Old French coste
    Norman côte

      Inherited from Old French coste, borrowed from Latin costa.

      Pronunciation

      [edit]
      • Audio (Jersey):(file)

      Noun

      [edit]

      côte f (plural côtes)

      1. (Jersey, geography) coast
      2. (Jersey) rib

      Derived terms

      [edit]
      • La Côte (“Gaspé”)
      • Côte d'Iviéthe (“Ivory Coast”)
